newsitem.title: MEXICO: Tribasa seeks joint rail bid with GMexico.
newsitem.headline: Tribasa seeks joint rail bid with GMexico.

text.p: Mexican construction company Grupo Tribasa SA de CV seeks to put forward a joint bid with mining giant Grupo Mexico SA (GMexico) in the auction for the operating concession of the Pacific North Rail line, a Tribasa director said Tuesday.
"We are in talks with them (GMexico) to put forward a joint proposal," the director said, asking not to be named.

Tribasa had formerly planned to bid for Mexico's largest railroad with U.S partner Burlington Northern, but submitted an application to operate the railroad with U.S. Railtex and Impulsora Tlaxcalteca de Industrias (ITISA) after Burlington opted out.
The Tribasa director said Burlington could still rejoin the railroad bid, "if it accepts the invitation."

Mexico accepted three applications for the railroad bidding on Friday, with a winner due to be declared on July 7. An alliance between Tribasa and Grupo Mexico would cut the competition to two, pitting the venture against Mexican builder ICA with U.S. Union Pacific Corp..

The more than 6,500-km line stretches from five U.S. border cities to ports on both coasts and the nation's three largest cities. The Pacific-North railroad carries about 45 percent of the nation's cargo.
